newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet, bid $67-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet, bid $67-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Wednesday were quiet amid light inquiry and no reported sales following Tuesday's active sales, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were light at $67.00 per cwt, but asking prices ranged from $68.00 to $70.00, they said.
About 30,000 head sold Tuesday at $68.00 in Kansas and about 36,000 to 38,000 sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma region, sources said.
Beef movement Tuesday was brisk but at lower prices, which could keep a lid on fed cattle prices.
Beef prices Tuesday were quoted down $0.70 to $2.37 per cwt, with the largest declines for choice beef, according to USDA. There were 276 fabricated loads sold.
Beef prices were pressured by mostly heavy offerings and moderate demand, with choice chuck and round cuts sharply lower, USDA said.
